assumptions: A single particle of mass m>0 is described by a complex scalar wavefunction Psi obeying the nonrelativistic Schrodinger equation with a real scalar potential; spinor and electromagnetic vector-potential couplings are outside this displayed form.
The spatial derivatives and local trajectory are considered in a region where Psi is sufficiently regular and nonzero. The displayed quotient is undefined at a node.

Locally write Psi=R exp(iS/hbar), with R=|Psi|>0 and a differentiable real phase S. The guidance law is equivalent there to dQ/dt=grad S/m; selecting this law is additional dynamical structure, not a unique consequence of the Schrodinger equation alone.
variables: Bold Q(t): the actual particle position, with the wavefunction ratio evaluated at x=Q(t); this position is not the scalar quantum potential Q on the companion card.
Psi(x,t): scalar wavefunction; m: particle mass; hbar: reduced Planck constant; grad: spatial gradient; Im: imaginary part.
patches.units: Both sides have units of velocity. Position Q has units of length; hbar/m has units of length squared per time, and grad Psi/Psi has units of inverse length.
patches.regime: Single-particle nonrelativistic scalar-wavefunction guidance without electromagnetic vector potential. An initially normalized Born distribution rho(x,t0)=|Psi(x,t0)|^2 is a separate statistical assumption: under the continuity dynamics and suitable regularity and boundary conditions it is preserved, not selected from arbitrary initial distributions by this equation. Many-particle, spinor and vector-potential forms require separately stated extensions.
patches.theoryRelationship: Equivalent local rewrite of the guidance/momentum restriction v=grad S/m in Bohm (1952), not a verbatim numbered quotient equation in the source.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 4, printed p. 169 / PDF p. 4, Eqs. (1)-(2): scalar one-particle Schrodinger equation with V(x), and Psi=R exp(iS/hbar). No electromagnetic vector potential appears in this displayed Hamiltonian.

Sec. 4, printed p. 170 / PDF p. 5: unnumbered v(x)=grad S(x)/m in the left column below Eq. (8), together with the continuity equations (5) and (7). Combining this velocity relation with Eq. (2) gives the card's quotient where Psi is nonzero.
Sec. 4, printed p. 171 / PDF p. 6: the ensemble-density discussion and the three numbered assumptions at the lower right distinguish the Schrodinger equation, p=grad S, and P=|Psi|^2.

assumptions: A single particle of mass m>0 is described by a complex scalar wavefunction Psi satisfying the nonrelativistic Schrodinger equation with a real scalar potential and no electromagnetic vector potential in this audited scope.
Use the local polar form Psi=R exp(iS/hbar), with R=|Psi|>0, twice spatially differentiable R, and sufficiently regular real phase S. The displayed division by R excludes nodes.

This term follows from the real part of the Schrodinger equation. No Born-equilibrium assumption or normalization is needed to form the local ratio; probabilistic ensemble claims require their own statistical assumptions.
variables: Q: scalar quantum potential, denoted U(x) in Bohm (1952), Eq. (8); it is not the bold particle position Q(t) on the guidance card.
R(x,t)=|Psi(x,t)|: nonnegative wave amplitude; S(x,t): local phase action; m: particle mass; hbar: reduced Planck constant; nabla squared: spatial Laplacian.
patches.units: Q has units of energy; S has units of action. The amplitude units cancel in (nabla squared R)/R, leaving inverse length squared.
patches.regime: The displayed scalar term is exact on smooth nonzero-amplitude regions of the declared single-particle model. It enters the modified Hamilton-Jacobi equation as partial S/partial t+(grad S)^2/(2m)+V+Q=0. At R=0 the quotient is undefined; this does not by itself imply that Q diverges on approach to every node. Many-particle, spinor and vector-potential settings are not audited by this card.
patches.theoryRelationship: The source's quantum-mechanical potential U is relabeled Q on this card; the displayed sign and factor match Eq. (8).

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 4, printed p. 169 / PDF p. 4, Eqs. (1)-(4): one-particle scalar Schrodinger equation, polar decomposition, and the real equation with the amplitude-curvature term.
Sec. 4, printed p. 170 / PDF p. 5, Eq. (8): U(x)=-(hbar squared/2m)(nabla squared R)/R. The card uses Q for the source's U; Eq. (8a) then uses V+U in the force law.
